title: Mother's AI query prompts genetic evaluation and a CDC42BPB diagnosis in a 22-month-old
summary: A smartphone app that the authors describe as powered by Google's Med-Gemini-3D suggested a rare skull finding that led to a genetic diagnosis in a 22-month-old; the app is unidentified.
account: On 15 May 2024 two Google research leaders introduced Med-Gemini-3D for computed tomography (CT) reports on the Google Research blog. They stated that Med-Gemini was not then a product offering available for commercial use. Hajebian and Friel (Journal of Craniofacial Surgery, published 16 January 2026) describe a 22-month-old girl with persistent bilateral parietal skull defects and global developmental delay. Her CT showed symmetric ossification defects beside the sagittal suture that the treating physician did not initially recognize. The mother used “a smartphone application powered by Med-Gemini-3D” on a three-dimensional CT reconstruction. It suggested “Catlin mark skull”, the historical name for enlarged parietal foramina. Genetic evaluation then identified a CDC42BPB variant associated with Chilton-Okur-Chung neurodevelopmental syndrome. The authors state that establishing the diagnosis facilitated earlier therapeutic interventions. The abstract notes that Google introduced Med-Gemini-3D in 2024 and that it is not approved for independent clinical use. The full text is paywalled. No cited source shows that a consumer app ran Med-Gemini-3D.
purpose: Consumer use of a CT-interpreting model to obtain a diagnosis for an unexplained skull finding

fields.account: On 15 May 2024 two Google research leaders introduced Med-Gemini-3D for computed tomography (CT) reports on the Google Research blog. They stated that Med-Gemini was not then a product offering available for commercial use. Hajebian and Friel (Journal of Craniofacial Surgery, published 16 January 2026) describe a 22-month-old girl with persistent bilateral parietal skull defects and global developmental delay. Her CT showed symmetric ossification defects beside the sagittal suture that the treating physician did not initially recognize. The mother used “a smartphone application powered by Med-Gemini-3D” on a three-dimensional CT reconstruction. It suggested “Catlin mark skull”, the historical name for enlarged parietal foramina. Genetic evaluation then identified a CDC42BPB variant associated with Chilton-Okur-Chung neurodevelopmental syndrome. The authors state that establishing the diagnosis facilitated earlier therapeutic interventions. The abstract notes that Google introduced Med-Gemini-3D in 2024 and that it is not approved for independent clinical use. The full text is paywalled. No cited source shows that a consumer app ran Med-Gemini-3D.
